diagnosis.message: Hello! Today we learn Express routes. When you type a website address with /books at the end, how does the server know what to send?

explain.message: Think of a big college office with counters: fees at one, certificates at another, library at a third. You go to the right counter for your work. Express routes are those counters. app.get with a path handles reading, app.post handles adding. Each route has a handler that gets req, the request, and res, the response. req.params holds parts of the path like a book id, req.body holds sent data. The handler sends back JSON with a status code, like 404 when a book is not found. Shall we build a library API?

example.message: A library API has app.get for /books/:id. The handler finds the book with req.params.id. If it is missing, it sends status 404 with an error. If found, res.json sends it. app.post on /books reads req.body and returns 201 Created. Why do we need express.json for the post route?

another_way.message: Another way: a railway station. Each platform number is a path, and the type of train, arriving or departing, is the method. A passenger, the request, goes to the right platform, and the station master, the handler, sends them on. What is the request method for adding new data?

not_understood.message: Step by step. One, create app with express. Two, write app.get with a path and a function. Three, inside, read req and send with res. Four, start with app.listen. What object do you use to send the answer back?

doubt.answer: Good doubt. Middleware runs before your handler, for every request or some. express.json is middleware that turns the request body into an object. Does that help?

questions: For a {context}, design two Express routes, one to read an item by id and one to add an item. Explain req, res and status codes.
In a {context}, a route returns 200 with empty data when the item does not exist. Explain what it should do instead and why.
Explain what middleware is in Express, with one example from a {context}.

feedback.good: You matched methods and paths to handlers correctly.
feedback.missing: Say what the handler sends back, including the right status code.
feedback.next: For each route: method, path, what it reads, what it sends.
